stumbles.quote: the centroid table costs 126 bytes per vector
stumbles.why: The arithmetic is not shown. 4096 centroids × dimension × bytes, divided by 100k, depends on the unstated dimension and precision. It is also unclear whether this is the 'more than a second bit per dimension' comparison.

stumbles.quote: If you partition a vector index with hash cells, learned centroids cut the scan fraction and raise coverage at the same time.
stumbles.why: This is framed as a general claim, but the evidence is one dataset at one size. It also says 'hash cells' as if they were the standard alternative.

point: On 100k EmbeddingGemma vectors, using 4,096 e-means (a faster k-means variant) centroids as index cells beats remex's hash cells on coverage and scan fraction. Offset coding also lifts recall, but at 100k vectors the centroid table's storage cost outweighs a cheaper second bit.
